# Password sign-in with optional TOTP

_sequence · source: `docs/atlas/views/sequence/sign-in.yaml`_

How a browser session is established. The refresh credential is a host-only HttpOnly cookie; browser JavaScript holds only the short-lived access token and a session-bound CSRF proof. TOTP, when enabled, turns the first response into a one-use MFA challenge.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor n_user as User
    participant n_flow as Sign-in flow (Web)
    participant n_provider as AuthProvider
    participant n_handler as AuthHandler
    participant n_limiter as Rate limiter
    participant n_service as AuthService
    participant n_catalog as users / refresh_tokens
    n_user->>n_flow: username, then password (or passkey)
    n_flow->>n_handler: POST /auth/login
    n_handler->>n_limiter: per-network and per-username fixed windows
    n_handler->>n_service: Login(username, password)
    n_service->>n_catalog: user lookup, bcrypt compare, MFA status
    alt TOTP enabled
        n_service-->>n_handler: one-use MFA challenge token (no session yet)
        n_handler-->>n_flow: mfa_required + challenge
        n_user->>n_flow: TOTP or recovery code
        n_flow->>n_handler: POST /auth/mfa/verify
        n_handler->>n_service: VerifyLoginMFA
    else password change required
        n_handler-->>n_flow: password-change challenge#59; session issued after POST /auth/password-change/complete
    end
    n_service->>n_catalog: store refresh session, update last login
    n_handler-->>n_flow: access token + CSRF in JSON, refresh token as HttpOnly cookie
    n_flow->>n_provider: store verified user and access token
    Note over n_provider,n_handler: Later requests send the access token as a Bearer header#59; AuthMiddleware authenticates each one. On expiry the client rotates the cookie under a cross-tab Web Lock.
    n_provider->>n_handler: POST /auth/refresh (cookie + CSRF)
```

## What the browser can and cannot read

The refresh credential never reaches JavaScript. Every session exit converges on `resetSession`, which removes credentials, resets feature and global state, clears user-scoped preferences, and clears the Query cache before another user signs in.
